results.evidence: The stored 16 pitches and 606 m describe the whole line from the ground (buttress to the bivy ledge, then the variation); the overview's six pitches counts only the detour that leaves the buttress at the bivy ledge. The route's own page says exactly this (a 6-pitch variation off the buttress, 2000 ft/16 pitches total). Nothing to correct.

The only source that describes the line (its own page) says 7 pitches in the header and 'nine pitches' in the text (455 m); the header and text are the same page so not independent. Searched summitpost (403), AAC/Alpinist, web searches for pitch count; no second source gives a count. No patch.

The overview's 'six long pitches on a 60 m rope' is one party's way of splitting the ~900 ft line into long leads; the listing's 11 pitches and the guidebook's nine are other ways of splitting the same crack. Splitting convention, not a contradiction; sources disagree among themselves (6/9/11) so no change is justified.

The route page describes about 300 m of solo slab approach, six long dihedral pitches to the Porcelain Chicken ledge, then several more pitches of loose rock to the summit on a 1,400 ft line; a second write-up likewise describes a six-pitch dihedral plus approach slabs. Both prove 1 is false but give no agreed count (the second says 7, the first implies more), so the header is blanked.

The route page's pitch-by-pitch text runs p1 to p13 (p13 is fourth class to trees, matching the row's descent text), and a magazine report on the Yak Peak classics calls it the 13-pitch Reality Check. Pitches set to 13.

Only the route's own listing (1000 ft/303 m, text mentions the step across on P2, no pitch count) describes it. Searched for other sources (thecrag, openbeta, supertopo, AAC East Face article, MP area): none mention Sheepish. Stored 1 pitch on a 305 m line is doubtful but no second source, so left.

results.fact: third-class ground before the first belay
results.evidence: The route page says 'fifty feet of easy third class' before the 3-bolt slab seam (matching the overview's 50 ft); the approach says about 100 feet. Searched AAC, openbeta mirror (404/same text), Alpinist, stephabegg: no independent source gives the figure. No patch.
The overview lists five pitch grades, the route's page and the area listing say 5 pitches (30-35 m each, 213 m line); a stored 0 is wrong on a five-pitch line.

results.fact: which route Airstream shares its start with
results.evidence: Both are true: the Solar Flare page says its first pitch is also the start for Airstream, and the same page says the Airstream/Sunspot line goes right at the bush where Solar Flare continues straight, so Airstream's opening is shared with Solar Flare's start and then with Sunspot Dihedral's line.
The route listing gives 11 pitches (grade V) and a magazine feature calls it an 11-pitch 5.13a/b. Stored 0 corrected.
The route page says pitch 1 holds all the climbing (~45 m, 61 m listed) and pitch 2 is an easy fourth/fifth-class scramble to the top; one climbing pitch is consistent with the stored 1.

Only the route's own page describes two pitches (jugs and bulge then a long plates-and-jugs pitch 2); searches of Mammoth Crest area pages, AAC new routes and general web found no second source. No patch.
